title: control-plane-phrasing-and-objection-scripts-for-financial-buyers
summary: Working draft: concise language and objection-rebuttal scripts tailored to regulated financial buyers evaluating a customer-managed control plane for LLM inference. Focus: how we phrase control plane responsibilities, auditability, data flows, and migration options so security/compliance/arch teams quickly understand risk boundaries and remediation levers.
audience: Security and compliance reviewers at banks, payment processors, and insurance firms; procurement and platform owners evaluating private (VPC/on-prem) inference options.
key_messages: 1) Clear separation: customer-managed control plane holds orchestration metadata only; sensitive data and model payloads remain in customer VPC or on-prem nodes. 2) Auditability first: we provide immutable, exportable audit logs and an integration path for your SIEM and archive retention policies. 3) Minimal trust surface: optional zero-knowledge telemetry, BYO-KMS for secrets, and configurable telemetry sampling. 4) Migration safe: same API and model/versioning semantics across hosted and private modes to reduce integration risk. 5) Operational SLA/response: dedicated runbook and optional managed response for incident triage with defined RTO/RPO for enterprise contracts.
phrasing_guidelines: - Use "customer-managed control plane" instead of "control plane in your network"; it emphasizes ownership and reduces anxiety about vendor visibility. - Avoid deep technical kernel jargon in sales decks for initial calls; say "orchestration metadata" and "no customer PII leaves your VPC unless explicitly configured." - For compliance reviewers: lead with audit artifacts (log formats, retention, export), encryption posture (in-transit + at-rest + BYO-KMS), and the ability to run full pen tests. - For architects: call out service boundaries (control plane, inference runtime, model store, telemetry) and show actual network flow diagram early in conversation. - Use simple analogies: "Redwood's control plane is like a scheduler — it tells your compute what to do but does not hold your private keys or raw documents."
detailed_scripts:
Opening (security reviewer): 'We understand your regulatory requirements. For the private deployment we propose a customer-managed control plane that keeps orchestration metadata outside of Redwood's hosted plane. All model payloads and token streams stay in your VPC/on-prem; you retain key control via your KMS/HSM.'

If asked about telemetry: 'Telemetry is opt-in and can be run in zero-knowledge mode where only non-identifying metrics are sent. Full logs are writable to your SIEM via our export adapters; we can also sign and timestamp audit bundles for offline retention.'

If asked about model updates and provenance: 'Models and version metadata can be pinned and signed by your team. We support cryptographic provenance for model artifacts and a rollout API that lets you canary and rollback within your private environment.'

Procurement-focused: 'We provide vendor-neutral SLAs for dedicated/private deployments and contract language for data residency and indemnity that aligns with typical financial buyer requirements (we'll surface specific clause templates on request).'"
objection_responses:
- 'We can't allow any external control plane touching our data' -> 'Understood. In our recommended configuration the control plane is deployed inside your VPC; if you prefer, the control plane is air-gapped and connected over a one-way export channel. No model payloads or PII transit to Redwood-hosted endpoints by default.'

- 'How do we prove nothing is exfiltrated?' -> 'We provide signed audit bundles, network-level flow logs, and a verifiable supply chain for model artifacts. We can also coordinate a joint pen-test and deliver an SBOM for all runtime components.'

- 'Vendor lock-in / migration fear' -> 'Same API layer across hosted and private modes; exportable model checkpoints, request logs, and deployment specs. We have migration runbooks and a sandbox migration engagement to validate you can move back to self-hosted or to another provider.'

- 'Regulators will want to see access controls and operator actions' -> 'Role-based access control with MFA, operator audit trails, and time-bound service accounts. We support granular separation of duties and can map logs to your identity provider for SSO and SCIM provisioning.'
competitive_notes:
- Cloud vendor managed endpoints: strength is perceived low-friction, weakness is limited control of audit artifacts and model provenance — emphasize Redwood's ability to run equivalent endpoints inside customer boundaries with stronger audit export.
- Pure OSS self-host: strength is full control; weakness is operational burden (patches, kernel tuning, batching optimizations). Redwood's angle: managed private deployment offering — we take operational runbooks and optimizations off their plate while preserving control of data/keys.
- Other managed private inference vendors: often require heavy agent installs or proprietary telemetry. Call out our pluggable telemetry adapters and BYO-KMS as differentiation. Also call out our unified API so dev teams don't need code changes when switching deployment modes.
- Pricing framing: some competitors present lower base cost but add 'ops uplift' — prepare TCO talking points showing engineer-hours saved for regulated deployments (include runbook examples in attachments).
rollout_guidance: - Suggested pilot: single model + canary traffic for non-customer-facing workflow (e.g., claims triage proof-of-concept) for 6 weeks. Deliverables: security design review, signed audit exports, one pen-test, migration runbook. - Stakeholders to include: InfoSec, AppSec, Platform Eng, Legal (data processing annex), and Procurement. - Decision gates: 1) Architecture sign-off; 2) Successful pen-test remediation; 3) SLA & contract clause agreement. - Post-pilot: offer a 3-month managed stabilization package and optional transfer of runbook artifacts to their SRE team.
open_questions_and_next_steps: - Confirm whether buyer requires air-gap or customer-managed control plane inside their VPC. - Get list of required regulatory attestations (PCI/GLBA/FFIEC/NYDFS) so we can map controls. - Ask Platform team for their preferred KMS/HSM integrations and SIEM endpoints. - Next step: prepare a 1-page architecture diagram customized to buyer's region and list of required regulatory clauses for legal to start drafting DPA addendum.
